mechanics.name: Solidarity
mechanics.currentEffect: While injured and healing another Survivor, you also gain healing progress at 65/70/75% speed.
activation: Be injured and heal another Survivor.
Ends/deactivates when: The self-healing progress effect ends when you stop healing another Survivor or are no longer injured.
mechanics.patchNote: Latest live balance change (10.2.0): Increased parallel self-healing progress from 50/60/70% to 65/70/75% and removed the no-Med-Kit restriction.
mechanics.plainEnglishSummary: While injured and healing a teammate, you also build your own healing progress at a reduced rate.
specialInteractions: The 10.2.0 live effect no longer requires healing without a Med-Kit.

editorial.summary: While injured, convert up to 75% of the healing you give another Survivor into progress on your own heal, including when using a Med-Kit.
useCases: Turn one teammate heal into substantial progress on your own health bar.
Combine two injured Survivors' reset needs into less total healing time.
Pair with strong altruistic healing bonuses so the shared reset becomes even faster.
counters: You must already be injured and heal another Survivor .
It never completes your own heal unless enough progress is generated or someone finishes it afterward.
If the team should remain injured and repair, healing at all can still be the wrong macro choice.
pros: Requires no token, cooldown, or special map object.
cons: Needs another injured Survivor to heal.
Does not help when you are the one receiving the heal first.
Still tied to the strategic value of healing in that match.
analysis: Solidarity became cleaner in 10.2. The conversion rate now reaches 75% and the old restriction against using a Med-Kit on the other Survivor is gone.
The perk still shines when two Survivors need a reset. One altruistic heal advances both health bars, reducing the total team time needed before both players can return to objectives.
Allowing Med-Kits broadens the build space because the user can accelerate the teammate heal with an Item without disabling Solidarity’s personal progress.
The buff is incremental rather than transformational, but it raises an already-efficient support perk and deserves consideration above its previous placement.
editorial.verdict: A better two-for-one heal in 10.2: 75% conversion and no Med-Kit restriction make Solidarity easier to exploit without changing its core job.
